domain_label: Plated Jewelry — Shape, Motif & Style-Family Systems for Producible, Convertible Form Selection
purpose: A method for choosing plated-jewelry shapes, motifs and style families that photograph and convert on-site/social AND stay producible at the owner's scale — by carrying a DESCRIPTIVE shape/motif/style-family taxonomy [FACT], a repeatable shape->conversion measurement [METHOD], and versatility/producibility/IP/cultural gates — while never inventing which shape 'sells best' or how popular a style family is (those stay [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN]).
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and all popularity/conversion magnitudes are labelled [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN], never asserted as measured

shape/motif/style-family NAMES and their describable visual attributes are treatable as [FACT-descriptive] (the vocabulary exists and is definable); their PREVALENCE, which converts, and which the 18-25 audience prefers are NOT facts and are only obtainable by the measurement methods this KB encodes
the owner runs a live website and paid IG/TikTok, so on-site product analytics, holdout/A-B tests and social engagement are the available signal sources; this KB encodes how to read each honestly

producibility is inherited from the supply-side vertical and the sibling kb1_category_construction_taxonomy: plating/forming complexity, plating-pass count and finding availability bound which shapes are makeable at the owner's scale; this KB accepts those constraints as input, it does not re-derive plating chemistry

finish (rhodium bright-white over silver, yellow/rose gold plating, two-tone) is a STYLE lever as much as a material choice; the precise FTC 16 CFR 23 finish definitions and rhodium's tarnish-resistant platinum-group properties are [FACT] carried from the materials specialist, not re-litigated here

IP/trademark/design-right and right-of-publicity law and cultural/religious-motif sensitivity are real constraints on motif choice, carried as binding [FACT-legal]/[FACT-ethics] flags, not waved through
exclusions: the category & construction taxonomy itself (studs/hoops/drops, chains/pendants, rings, bracelets, anklets) and its plating/forming derivation — the sibling kb1_category_construction_taxonomy owns that; this KB works ACROSS categories on shape/motif/style

sizing, fit tolerance and the sizing->returns mechanics (ring sizing, chain lengths, post gauges) — the sibling kb3_sizing_fit_returns owns those; this KB only flags the shape->returns link and hands off

the actual demand read, brand landscape, price tiers and consumer segmentation (the market specialist S1) and the poll instrument (the poll specialist S4); this KB consumes their signals, it does not produce the market numbers

the final SKU pick / launch set of six (the assortment specialist S5) and the unit economics / pricing (the economics specialist S6); this KB stops at a ranked, producible, on-brand, testable shape/style shortlist

asserting any specific market share, popularity percentage, competitor design claim, or 'best-selling shape' as measured fact; those are produced later by the polls and public-data pulls the methods here direct

glossary.definition: The primitive geometric form of a piece read at a glance (round/hoop, stud/point, linear/bar/paperclip, teardrop/pear, heart, star/celestial, cross, organic/freeform, geometric, floral); a [FACT-descriptive] vocabulary — naming a silhouette is definable and objective, whereas claiming a silhouette 'sells best' is not a fact and requires the conversion method.

The representational subject applied to a silhouette (celestial, floral/botanical, heart, evil-eye, initial/letter, serpent, butterfly, shell/coastal, zodiac, animal); some motifs carry cultural/religious or IP weight and are gated before use.

A named aesthetic grouping defined by describable attributes: minimalist/delicate (thin, small-scale, negative space), statement/bold (oversize, high-contrast), Y2K (butterfly/heart/charm, mixed metals), coastal/coquette (shell, pearl, bow, warm gold), edgy/gothic (serpent, spike, matte/black), classic/timeless (hoop, tennis, solitaire), boho (organic, textured, layered). The family names and attributes are [FACT-descriptive]; their popularity, size, and conversion are [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD], never asserted as measured.

The repeatable procedure for attributing on-site conversion to a shape: product-level view->add-to-cart->purchase funnels segmented by silhouette, holdout/A-B or waitlist tests, and confound controls (price band, photo quality, grid placement, seasonality). Output is a labelled [ESTIMATE] with a confidence and sample-size caveat, never a bare 'this shape converts best'.

Imaging principles that make a piece read well in a small feed/PDP thumbnail: silhouette legibility (an unambiguous outline at ~150px), contrast against skin and background, controlled reflectivity of bright rhodium/gold finishes, and a clear on-body scale reference. These are UX/imaging facts; the link from photogenic to purchase is an [ESTIMATE] validated only by the conversion method.

A design property whereby a piece is worn in multiples or combinations (stacking rings, layered necklaces, curated ear stacks of studs/huggies) or across occasions; it is a real design lever that tends to raise units-per-order and AOV [ESTIMATE on magnitude] and underpins collection cohesion.

The bound on which shapes/motifs are makeable at the owner's scale, inherited from the supply-side vertical and kb1: openwork/pave/fine-relief/undercut geometries, plating-pass count, two-tone masking, sharp edges that wear plating, and finding availability all raise cost or make a form impractical; a shape that cannot be plated/formed cleanly is cut or simplified regardless of appeal.

Finish is an aesthetic choice, not only a material one: bright-white rhodium over sterling silver (a hard, tarnish-resistant platinum-group finish [FACT]) reads modern/minimalist; warm yellow/rose gold plating reads classic/coastal; two-tone signals a specific look but costs extra plating passes/masking. FTC 16 CFR 23 defines the finish terms (gold-plated, vermeil = >=10k gold >=2.5um over sterling, rhodium) [FACT].

The test that separates a durable silhouette (hoop, stud, huggie, paperclip chain, tennis) from a decaying fad motif (a specific viral charm): breadth across audiences, longevity of the signal, cross-platform persistence, and whether demand attaches to a timeless silhouette versus a single fad motif; used to decide what belongs in the durable launch core versus a small fad test.

A binding pre-design check: generic shapes and common motifs are free to use, but copying a fashion house's signature motif/trade-dress, a trademarked symbol, or a protected design is infringement risk, and religious/cultural/sacred motifs (and appropriation) must be cleared for sensitivity; 'AI-designed' does not launder a copied signature or a sacred symbol.

nodes.definition: Encode the METHOD to MEASURE whether a shape converts, replacing any guess. This is the honest answer to the owner's 'which shape do I need' — a way to find out, not an invented ranking.

nodes.definition: Encode how to read social engagement (saves, shares, watch-time, comment sentiment, IG/TikTok reach) as a shape-preference proxy, and its biases. Engagement is a cheap, fast, top-of-funnel signal of visual appeal, but it is a VANITY-vs-PURCHASE-INTENT proxy: saves and likes measure 'I find this striking', not 'I will buy this', and platform algorithms, giveaway incentives (which the poll specialist covers) and creator amplification distort it. The method: treat engagement as a directional filter that nominates shapes to TEST, weighted below actual on-site conversion; prefer save/share (intent-leaning) over like (passive); watch for the aspirational-statement bias where bold, un-producible or un-affordable pieces over-index on engagement but under-index on purchase. Output is a ranked shortlist of candidate shapes to feed into SHAPE_CONVERSION_METHOD and TREND_DURABILITY_DISCRIMINATOR — never a purchase claim on its own.

nodes.definition: Establish the scale/proportion system linking physical size (mm) to both thumbnail legibility and wearability, because the same silhouette behaves differently at different scales. Small/micro (delicate studs ~3-6mm, thin ~1mm chains) read minimalist, layer and stack well, and are light/comfortable, but can vanish at thumbnail scale and need macro/on-body shots. Mid-scale (hoops ~20-40mm, pendants ~15-25mm) balance legibility and wearability. Oversize/statement (large hoops >50mm, chunky pendants) dominate a thumbnail and read bold, but add weight, can pull on ear piercings, snag, and drive comfort-based returns (bridged to SHAPE_RETURNS_LINK and the sibling kb3). Scale is also a style-family signal (micro=minimalist, oversize=statement) and a producibility/cost driver (more metal, more plating area). The method: specify a target mm range per shape tied to its style intent, its thumbnail legibility need, and its wearability/return risk — never optimize a hero image at a scale nobody wears.

nodes.definition: Establish versatility/stackability as a design property [FACT-design] and a units-per-order/AOV lever [ESTIMATE on magnitude]. A versatile piece is worn in multiples or combinations — stacking rings, layered necklaces of graduated lengths, curated ear stacks of studs/huggies/climbers, mix-and-match charms — or across occasions (day-to-night). Stackable/layerable forms tend to raise units-per-order (a shopper buying three stacking rings not one) and support collection cohesion and repeat purchase, which is why delicate, modular, small-scale silhouettes are strategically valuable beyond their per-unit appeal. This is a genuine merchandising design principle; the SIZE of the AOV lift is an [ESTIMATE] to be validated by on-site basket analysis, not asserted. The method: score each candidate shape for stack/layer compatibility and occasion versatility, and prefer, other things equal, forms that compose into multi-unit purchases and coherent collections. Versatility also tensions against statement pieces (STYLE_FAMILY_TAXONOMY), which sell as singular hero items.

nodes.definition: Establish finish/colorway as a STYLE lever, not only a material choice, with its plating-pass cost. nodes.definition: Encode the METHOD to separate a DURABLE silhouette from a decaying FAD motif, so the launch core is not built on something that dies before the plating run lands. Durable forms (hoops, studs, huggies, paperclip/curb chains, tennis, solitaire, simple pendants) show breadth across audiences, multi-year longevity, cross-platform persistence, and demand attached to a timeless SILHOUETTE. Fads (a specific viral charm, a single-season motif spike) show narrow, spiky, single-platform, motif-specific signals that decay fast. The discriminators: signal breadth (many audiences vs one niche), longevity (sustained vs spike-and-drop), cross-platform persistence, and silhouette-vs-motif attachment (a durable silhouette survives a motif's fade). The method routes durable forms into the launch core and caps fad motifs at a small, cheap, fast test allocation — because a plating/forming run committed to a fad that has already peaked becomes dead stock. All durability calls are [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD], not certainty; a fad can persist and a 'durable' form can soften.

nodes.definition: Carry the binding cultural/religious motif-sensitivity gate [FACT-ethics]. Some motifs in the lexicon carry meaning beyond decoration: religious symbols (cross, hamsa, Om, Star of David), the evil-eye/nazar (protective, culturally specific), sacred or Indigenous imagery, and culturally loaded animals/symbols. Using these decoratively risks offense, appropriation backlash and brand damage, especially for a young, socially-active audience. The method: for each motif, check whether it is religious/sacred/culturally specific; if so, decide honestly whether the brand has standing and intent to use it respectfully, prefer secular/geometric alternatives when unsure, and never use sacred imagery as a throwaway trend piece. 'AI-designed' does not launder a culturally loaded motif. This is an ethics-and-brand-risk gate applied BEFORE render/test/production, not a market-size question; it is a genuine constraint the factory must not wave through.

nodes.definition: Carry the binding IP/originality gate [FACT-legal]. Generic shapes (a plain hoop, a round stud, a paperclip chain) and common motifs (a simple heart, a star) are free to use, but three exposures must be cleared before design/render/production: (1) copying a fashion house's SIGNATURE motif or trade-dress (a recognizable proprietary pattern/lock/clover-type signature) risks trademark/trade-dress infringement; (2) reproducing a TRADEMARKED symbol/logo or a protected character is infringement; (3) copying a specific competitor's protected DESIGN (design patent / registered design, where applicable) is actionable. Additionally, right-of-publicity applies if a real person's name/likeness is used (routed to the same discipline as the sweater KB's legal flag). The method: for each candidate motif/shape, verify it is generic or original, and if it echoes a recognizable house signature or mark, redesign to a generic form or clear it — 'AI-designed' does NOT launder a copied signature. This gate runs before the cheap tests, because testing or producing an infringing form wastes the spend and creates liability.

nodes.definition: Resolve the central tension of this KB: a shape can be high-appeal (photogenic, high-engagement, on-trend) yet low-producibility (intricate, multi-pass, sharp/thin, hard to plate cleanly at scale). The rule is value engineering of FORM: (1) if a high-appeal shape is un-producible at the owner's scale, first attempt to SIMPLIFY it to a producible form that keeps the appeal signal (reduce openwork, thicken thin sections, drop a plating pass, standardize findings); (2) if it cannot be simplified without losing the appeal, CUT it from the launch core and, at most, allocate a small test; (3) never commit a run to a shape that cannot be plated/formed cleanly, because a defect-prone or wear-through form damages the brand and returns more than its appeal earns. This mirrors the materials specialist's 'lower cost without lowering quality' but for geometry: keep the look, remove the un-makeable detail. Producibility (PRODUCIBILITY_CONSTRAINT_MAP) and appeal (SHAPE_CONVERSION_METHOD/PHOTOGENIC) are both inputs; producibility is a hard gate, appeal is an optimization within it.

nodes.definition: Flag the link from shape choice to return/exchange risk, bridging to the sibling kb3_sizing_fit_returns without owning the sizing mechanics. edges.why_related: how well a shape photographs causally influences its click and add-to-cart rate in a visual feed/PDP, though the effect must be measured not assumed
render/waitlist test results feed back to sharpen the family-audience fit estimate before any run
both are binding pre-design motif-clearance gates that must pass before render/test/production, differing only in the exposure (legal vs cultural)

conflict_axes.name: appeal_vs_producibility
conflict_axes.description: The most photogenic/high-converting shape can be the least producible at the owner's scale (openwork, pave, sharp/thin, multi-pass), so form appeal and makeability pull against each other.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: producibility is a hard gate, appeal an optimization within it: simplify the high-appeal shape to a producible form keeping the appeal, else cut it from the core

conflict_axes.name: statement_vs_minimalist
conflict_axes.description: Bold statement pieces drive discovery, social reach and singular hero sales, while delicate minimalist/stackable forms drive units-per-order, AOV and everyday repeat; a line skewed fully to either loses the other's benefit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: anchor with one statement hero for reach and build depth in versatile stackable forms for basket size

conflict_axes.name: fad_vs_durable
conflict_axes.description: A viral fad motif (Y2K spike, a single-season charm) shows the strongest, fastest signal but decays before a plating run pays back, while a durable silhouette (hoop, stud, huggie) sustains demand.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route durable silhouettes into the launch core and cap fad motifs at a small cheap fast test allocation

conflict_axes.name: engagement_vs_conversion
conflict_axes.description: Social engagement (saves, likes, shares) is fast and cheap but is a vanity/aspirational-intent proxy, while on-site conversion is the real purchase signal but slower and traffic-limited.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight measured conversion above engagement; use engagement only to nominate shapes to test

conflict_axes.name: photogenic_vs_wearable
conflict_axes.description: A shape optimized for a thumbnail hero (oversize, high-contrast) can be uncomfortable or return-prone to wear, while a comfortable everyday scale can under-read at thumbnail size.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: specify a scale that stays wearable and use macro/on-body shots for legibility; weigh comfort-return risk against thumbnail impact

conflict_axes.name: finish_variety_vs_operational_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: Offering multiple finishes/colorways (rhodium, gold, rose, two-tone) stretches one silhouette across style families but multiplies SKUs, plating passes and inventory.
poles: offer many finishes for style range
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use finish as a style lever only where it reinforces a target family, counting each finish's plating-pass and SKU cost

conflict_axes.name: cohesive_focus_vs_broad_coverage
conflict_axes.description: A tightly cohesive single-family capsule cross-sells and reads as a brand but is fragile to that family's fade, while broad coverage hedges trend risk but competes with itself and dilutes identity.
poles: cover a broad range of families
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lead with a cohesive core in one-or-two audience-fit families plus a small hedge, sharing a form language

conflict_axes.name: expressive_motif_vs_ip_cultural_risk
conflict_axes.description: A distinctive, expressive motif (a recognizable signature-like pattern, a loaded cultural/religious symbol) can be the most appealing yet carry trademark/trade-dress or appropriation risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: clear IP and cultural exposure before design/test; redesign a signature echo to a generic original and avoid sacred imagery as a trend piece

conflict_axes.name: measured_signal_vs_founder_taste
conflict_axes.description: A tested [ESTIMATE] of what converts can conflict with the founder's aesthetic conviction, tempting a taste-driven pick over the data or a data pick that ignores brand vision.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lead with the tested signal for the core, reserving a small founder-taste allocation as an explicitly-labelled bet, never overriding a clear signal

edge_cases.description: A fashion house's signature motif or trade-dress (a recognizable clover/lock/pattern) is copied on the assumption it is a generic shape
edge_cases.trigger: a candidate motif echoes a recognizable house signature without an IP clearance
edge_cases.mitigation: run the IP gate before render/test: redesign the echo to a generic original or clear it; 'AI-designed' does not launder a copied signature

edge_cases.description: A sacred/religious or culturally loaded motif is used as a throwaway trend piece, triggering appropriation backlash
edge_cases.trigger: a design applies a religious/sacred/culturally-specific motif decoratively without a sensitivity check
edge_cases.mitigation: run the cultural gate before design; prefer secular/geometric alternatives when unsure and never use sacred imagery as a trend charm

edge_cases.description: A shape that photographs beautifully at thumbnail is oversize/heavy and returns for comfort
edge_cases.trigger: a shape is selected on thumbnail hero appeal at a statement scale nobody comfortably wears
edge_cases.mitigation: specify a wearable target mm range, use macro/on-body shots for legibility, and weigh comfort-return risk against thumbnail impact

edge_cases.description: A viral Y2K fad motif is committed to a full plating run and peaks before the run lands, becoming dead stock
edge_cases.trigger: a fad motif with a spiky single-platform signal is allocated to the launch core
edge_cases.mitigation: cap fad motifs at a small cheap fast test and anchor the core on durable silhouettes

edge_cases.description: IG saves/likes are read as purchase intent and a shape nobody buys is committed
edge_cases.trigger: an engagement-nominated aspirational-statement shape is treated as a conversion decision
edge_cases.mitigation: weight measured on-site conversion above engagement and pre-test the shape via waitlist before any run

edge_cases.description: An intricate openwork/pave motif is chosen that the owner's plating/forming cannot render cleanly at scale
edge_cases.trigger: a high-appeal low-producibility shape enters the core without the producibility gate
edge_cases.mitigation: apply simplify-then-cut: reduce openwork/thicken sections to a producible form keeping the appeal, else cut from the core

edge_cases.description: A single-point 'this shape converts best' claim is made without a holdout/test
edge_cases.trigger: a bestseller rank or a small sample is reported as a measured shape-conversion fact
edge_cases.mitigation: report shape conversion as a labelled [ESTIMATE] with confidence and sample caveat, controlling price/photo/ad-spend confounds

edge_cases.description: A style-family popularity or a demographic/ethnic purchase preference is asserted as fact to satisfy the owner's question
edge_cases.trigger: an un-measured 'which style/ethnicity buys' number is stated as measured
edge_cases.mitigation: give the measurement method (poll, ad test, public data) or an honest [UNKNOWN]; never a guess, and route demographic segmentation to the market specialist's method ethics

edge_cases.description: A thin/delicate shape bends or wears through its plating fast, generating quality complaints
edge_cases.trigger: a very thin/sharp form is chosen without the durability/plating-wear check
edge_cases.mitigation: thicken thin sections and soften sharp edges to a durable, cleanly-platable form; route plating-wear detail to the materials specialist

edge_cases.description: A two-tone/specialty finish reads on-brand but doubles plating passes and blows up cost/SKU count
edge_cases.trigger: finish variety is treated as free styling without counting plating-pass and SKU cost
edge_cases.mitigation: use finish as a style lever only where it reinforces a target family, counting each finish's plating-pass and inventory cost

edge_cases.description: All six launch items are chosen in one style family, leaving the line fragile to that aesthetic cooling
edge_cases.trigger: the cohesion drive over-narrows to a single family with no hedge
edge_cases.mitigation: lead with a cohesive one-or-two-family core plus a small hedge sharing a form language, per the assortment specialist's coverage-vs-depth

edge_cases.description: The founder's taste overrides a clear tested conversion signal and picks a shape with no demand
edge_cases.trigger: a taste-driven pick displaces a shape with a strong measured signal
edge_cases.mitigation: lead the core with the tested signal and reserve a small explicitly-labelled founder-taste bet, never overriding a clear signal

workflow.description: Enumerate the primitive silhouette classes as a category-independent [FACT-descriptive] alphabet, noting naming is not a selling claim
workflow.gate: the silhouette classes are enumerated as a descriptive alphabet with the naming-is-not-selling note

workflow.description: Enumerate the motif classes orthogonal to silhouette and style, flagging cultural- and IP-loaded motifs for the gates
workflow.gate: the motif classes are enumerated with loaded motifs routed to the cultural and IP gate nodes

workflow.description: Define each family by its silhouette/motif/scale/finish attributes as [FACT-descriptive], tagging popularity/conversion claims [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]
workflow.gate: each family is defined by attributes with all popularity/conversion claims tagged [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]

workflow.description: Score each silhouette/motif for makeability (openwork, pave, relief, sharp/thin, two-tone, findings) using inherited plating/forming constraints
workflow.gate: each candidate shape carries a producibility score with low-producibility forms flagged

workflow.description: State thumbnail legibility/contrast/reflectivity/on-body heuristics and target mm scales, with the photogenic-is-not-converting boundary
workflow.gate: the imaging heuristics and target scales are stated with the photogenic != converts boundary

workflow.description: Specify per-shape funnel segmentation, holdout/waitlist tests and confound controls, outputting a labelled [ESTIMATE]
workflow.gate: the measurement plan outputs a labelled [ESTIMATE] with confidence and forbids a bare best-shape claim

workflow.action: Read social signal and split durable vs fad
workflow.description: Use engagement as a weighted nomination filter and apply breadth/longevity/silhouette-vs-motif discriminators to split durable from fad
workflow.gate: durable forms are routed to the core and fads capped at a small test, all calls [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]

workflow.action: Score versatility, scale and return risk
workflow.description: Score stack/layer/occasion versatility (AOV lever as [ESTIMATE]) and return-risk shape features, routing sizing mechanics to kb3
workflow.gate: each shape carries stackability and return-risk scores with the AOV lift labelled [ESTIMATE]

workflow.description: Render/mockup, merch-grid/ad-test and waitlist the finalists (only cleared, producible shapes) to capture appeal before any run
workflow.gate: finalists are pre-tested as a directional [ESTIMATE], gated by producibility and IP/cultural clearance

workflow.description: Run the generic-vs-signature IP check and the religious/cultural-sensitivity check before design/test/production
workflow.gate: every candidate has an IP and cultural clearance pass/fail before it proceeds

workflow.action: Resolve appeal-vs-producibility and cohere the collection
workflow.description: Apply simplify-then-cut to high-appeal low-producibility shapes and select a subset sharing a form language with a statement anchor
workflow.gate: high-appeal shapes are simplified-or-cut to producible forms and the group shares a form language

workflow.description: Deliver the ranked producible/on-brand/testable shortlist with tags, scores, clearance and labelled [ESTIMATE] signal, stopping before the SKU/price/demand decision
workflow.gate: the ranked cleared producible shortlist with binding conditions is delivered with a clean boundary before S5/S6

priority_rationale: The shape vocabulary, motif lexicon and style-family taxonomy come first because every downstream method indexes into this descriptive alphabet; producibility, photogenics, scale and the conversion/social measurement methods come next because they are the gates and signal sources the selection reasons over; versatility, trend-durability, the pre-production test, the audience map and the IP/cultural gates then turn signal into gated, tested candidates; and the appeal-vs-producibility tradeoff, returns link, cohesion logic, honesty ledger and hand-off come last because they compose the ranked, producible, cleared, on-brand shortlist and its clean boundary before the assortment and economics specialists.

dominance_rules.rationale: a shape that cannot be plated/formed cleanly at scale ships defects and returns more than its appeal earns
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-appeal shape scores low on producibility
dominance_rules.action: simplify it to a producible form keeping the appeal, else cut it from the launch core

dominance_rules.rule: Measured on-site conversion dominates social engagement
dominance_rules.rationale: engagement is a vanity/aspirational proxy while conversion is the real purchase signal
dominance_rules.trigger: engagement and conversion disagree on a shape
dominance_rules.action: act on the measured conversion [ESTIMATE] and use engagement only to nominate shapes to test

dominance_rules.rule: Durable silhouette dominates fad motif for the launch core
dominance_rules.rationale: a plating run committed to a peaked fad becomes dead stock
dominance_rules.trigger: a fad motif shows a strong but spiky single-platform signal
dominance_rules.action: anchor the core on durable silhouettes and cap the fad at a small cheap fast test

dominance_rules.rule: IP and cultural clearance dominate distinctiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: an infringing or appropriative motif creates legal liability and brand damage that outweigh its appeal
dominance_rules.trigger: a distinctive motif echoes a house signature/mark or a loaded cultural symbol
dominance_rules.action: redesign to a generic original or avoid it; do not test or produce an un-cleared motif

dominance_rules.rule: Tested signal dominates founder taste for the core
dominance_rules.rationale: an invented or taste-driven pick without a signal risks the launch on conviction
dominance_rules.trigger: founder taste conflicts with a clear tested conversion signal
dominance_rules.action: lead the core with the tested signal and reserve a small explicitly-labelled founder-taste bet

dominance_rules.rule: The honest band dominates any single-point popularity/conversion claim
dominance_rules.rationale: which shape/style sells is un-measured until tested, so a point figure is unsupportable
dominance_rules.trigger: a best-shape or style-popularity number is stated as measured
dominance_rules.action: carry a labelled [ESTIMATE] with confidence or an honest [UNKNOWN], never a guess

dominance_rules.rule: Wearability/return risk dominates thumbnail photogenics when they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: a comfort-return-prone shape can be net-negative despite strong thumbnail appeal
dominance_rules.trigger: a thumbnail-optimized shape carries high comfort/return risk
dominance_rules.action: specify a wearable scale and weigh return risk against the conversion estimate before committing

dominance_rules.rule: Stackability/versatility breaks ties among equally-converting shapes
dominance_rules.rationale: versatile stackable forms raise units-per-order and collection cohesion
dominance_rules.trigger: two candidate shapes have comparable conversion estimates
dominance_rules.action: prefer the more stack/layer-compatible form, other things equal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Score producibility before investing photography, sampling or a plating run in a shape
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tooling or shooting an intricate shape that cannot be made cleanly and must be scrapped at sampling

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear IP and cultural exposure before any design, render or test spend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending on and producing an infringing or appropriative motif that draws liability and backlash and must be pulled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every style-family popularity and shape-conversion claim [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented popularity/best-shape number circulating as fact and having to be retracted against the honesty contract

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set up the shape->conversion measurement (funnel/holdout/waitlist) before claiming a shape converts
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing a run on a confounded bestseller rank and re-doing the selection once the confound surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Split durable vs fad before committing a plating/forming run to a motif
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full run on a peaked fad becoming dead stock that ties up capital and inventory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide finish/colorway as a style lever with its plating-pass cost before pricing and SKU planning
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a finish-variety SKU explosion discovered only after pricing, forcing a re-plan of the launch set

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the collection's shared shape/motif/finish language before picking individual pieces
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an incoherent set that competes with itself and must be re-composed after selection

anti_rework_rules.rule: Specify a wearable target mm scale and check return-risk features before shooting thumbnail-optimized hero images
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a hero-optimized oversize shape that returns for comfort and must be re-scaled and re-shot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the cheap pre-production render/waitlist test before tooling or a plating run
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying for tooling and a run on a shape that a near-zero-cost test would have shown was weak

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shape->conversion test or holdout completes and returns a per-shape estimate
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank the candidate shapes and update the shortlist and audience map

iteration_protocol.trigger: a trend signal spikes or decays across a season
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the durable-vs-fad discriminator and re-allocate core versus fad-test

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner's plating/forming capability or supplier set changes, or a live forming/plating quote lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-map producibility and re-resolve the appeal-vs-producibility tradeoff

iteration_protocol.trigger: the poll (S4) or a paid-social test returns a category/style-family preference
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the style-family-to-audience estimate and re-cohere the collection

iteration_protocol.trigger: an IP or cultural flag is raised on a candidate motif
iteration_protocol.action: pull or redesign the motif and re-cohere the affected collection

iteration_protocol.trigger: a returns spike ties to a specific shape feature (oversize, sharp, thin, fit-dependent)
iteration_protocol.action: update the shape-returns link and re-weigh the shape against its conversion estimate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a pre-production render/waitlist test returns a signal or diverges from realized purchase
iteration_protocol.action: update the cheap-test read and the conversion estimate before any run
